Sample.evidence_source: The DLS comprises six items (e.g., "My goal is to have well-toned muscles"), rated from 1 = never to 6 = always. Item scores are averaged; higher scores reflect higher levels of drive for leanness. Item scores have demonstrated internal reliability and construct validity in U.S. undergraduate (Smolak & Murnen, 2008) and Australian community (De Jesus et al., 2015) men; internal reliability has also been demonstrated among gay men in the U.S. (Strubel & Petrie, 2018).

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Drive for Leanness Scale (DLS): a six-item measure rated 1 (never) to 6 (always), with averaged item scores where higher scores indicate greater drive for leanness. It notes that the DLS has demonstrated internal reliability and construct validity in prior samples (U.S. undergraduates; Australian community men) and internal reliability among gay men in the U.S.; no study-specific sample, methods, or statistics are reported here.
